doc.title: Mat Domber interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, January 12, 2007

title: Growing up on records and Eddie Condon, Pee Wee Russell, Muggsy Spanier
summary: His father's radio with Benny Goodman records, then Nick's and the Condon crowd as a young fan.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Growing up with radio, records and family listening

blocks.x: Yeah. Was the music, this kind of music, prevalent in your house when you were growing up?

Yeah. From the time I was maybe eight or nine years old my father bought a radio and in those days it had a victrola attachment to it, and in those days when they sold those things they also had records that went along with it. So one of the first things that we had in our house was the “Overture of William Tell” and Benny Goodman, some of the early Benny Goodman trios and quartets and some of the big band stuff. And I started to listen to that. Then I became an Eddie Condonite. And before I was old enough to be able to drink, my father, who liked to have his little Seagrams and Seven you know, and that sort of thing, we used to be down to Nick’s and he didn’t like the music particularly but he knew that I appreciated it and he used to stand there at the bar and I tried to emulate Pee Wee Russell
